claim: Npnt mRNA and protein are expressed by various ocular tissues during chick corneal development.
source: We found that Npnt mRNA and protein are expressed by various ocular tissues, including the migratory periocular neural crest (pNC), which also express the integrin alpha 8 (Itgα8) receptor.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 1 and described in the text.

claim: Migratory periocular neural crest (pNC) express the integrin alpha 8 (Itgα8) receptor.
source: We found that Npnt mRNA and protein are expressed by various ocular tissues, including the migratory periocular neural crest (pNC), which also express the integrin alpha 8 (Itgα8) receptor.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data showing Itgα8 expression in pNC as shown in Figure 3.

claim: Knockdown of Npnt attenuated cornea development.
source: Knockdown of either Npnt or Itgα8 attenuated cornea development, whereas overexpression of Npnt resulted in cornea thickening.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced corneal thickness following Npnt knockdown as shown in Figure 2.

claim: Knockdown of Itgα8 attenuated cornea development.
source: Knockdown of either Npnt or Itgα8 attenuated cornea development, whereas overexpression of Npnt resulted in cornea thickening.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced corneal thickness following Itgα8 knockdown as shown in Figure 4.

claim: Overexpression of Npnt resulted in cornea thickening.
source: Knockdown of either Npnt or Itgα8 attenuated cornea development, whereas overexpression of Npnt resulted in cornea thickening.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing increased corneal thickness following Npnt overexpression as shown in Figure 5.

claim: Overexpression of Npnt variants lacking RGD-binding sites did not affect corneal thickness.
source: Moreover, overexpression of Npnt variants lacking RGD-binding sites did not affect corneal thickness.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing no change in corneal thickness with RGD mutant or truncated Npnt as shown in Figure 6.

claim: Neither the knockdown nor augmentation of Npnt caused significant changes in cell proliferation.
source: Neither the knockdown nor augmentation of Npnt caused significant changes in cell proliferation, suggesting that Npnt directs pNC migration into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU proliferation assays shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Npnt directs pNC migration into the cornea.
source: Neither the knockdown nor augmentation of Npnt caused significant changes in cell proliferation, suggesting that Npnt directs pNC migration into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Npnt affects corneal thickness without affecting proliferation, combined with in vitro migration data.

claim: Npnt promotes pNC migration from explanted periocular mesenchyme.
source: In vitro analyses showed that Npnt promotes pNC migration from explanted periocular mesenchyme, which requires Itgα8, focal adhesion kinase, and Rho kinase.
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assays shown in Figures 3 and 7.

claim: Npnt-promoted pNC migration requires Itgα8.
source: In vitro analyses showed that Npnt promotes pNC migration from explanted periocular mesenchyme, which requires Itgα8, focal adhesion kinase, and Rho kinase.
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assays with α8β1 inhibitor shown in Figure 3.

claim: Npnt-promoted pNC migration requires focal adhesion kinase.
source: In vitro analyses showed that Npnt promotes pNC migration from explanted periocular mesenchyme, which requires Itgα8, focal adhesion kinase, and Rho kinase.
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assays with FAK inhibitor shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Npnt-promoted pNC migration requires Rho kinase.
source: In vitro analyses showed that Npnt promotes pNC migration from explanted periocular mesenchyme, which requires Itgα8, focal adhesion kinase, and Rho kinase.
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assays with ROCK inhibitor shown in Figure 7.

claim: Npnt augments cell migration into the presumptive cornea extracellular matrix by functioning as a substrate for Itgα8-positive pNC cells.
source: Combined, these data suggest that Npnt augments cell migration into the presumptive cornea extracellular matrix by functioning as a substrate for Itgα8-positive pNC cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of knockdown, overexpression, and in vitro migration experiments.

claim: The cornea comprises three cellular layers: epithelium, stroma, and endothelium.
source: In vertebrates, the cornea comprises three cellular layers: epithelium, stroma, and endothelium.
evidence: This is established knowledge about corneal anatomy.

claim: The corneal epithelium is derived from the ectoderm.
source: The corneal epithelium is derived from the ectoderm, whereas the stromal keratocytes and corneal endothelium are derived from cranial neural crest cells (Lwigale et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The stromal keratocytes and corneal endothelium are derived from cranial neural crest cells.
source: The corneal epithelium is derived from the ectoderm, whereas the stromal keratocytes and corneal endothelium are derived from cranial neural crest cells (Lwigale et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In birds and humans, neural crest migration from the periocular region into the presumptive cornea occurs in two waves.
source: In birds and humans, neural crest migration from the periocular region into the presumptive cornea occurs in two waves (Feneck et al., 2020; Hay, 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The first wave of neural crest migration forms a monolayer of the nascent corneal endothelium.
source: The first wave forms a monolayer of the nascent corneal endothelium, which is accompanied by a second wave of mesenchymal migration into the acellular matrix between endothelium and ectoderm to form the cornea stroma (Hay and Revel, 1969; Noden, 1978; Lwigale et al., 2005; Creuzet et al., 2005; Feneck et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The second wave of neural crest migration involves mesenchymal migration into the acellular matrix between endothelium and ectoderm to form the cornea stroma.
source: The first wave forms a monolayer of the nascent corneal endothelium, which is accompanied by a second wave of mesenchymal migration into the acellular matrix between endothelium and ectoderm to form the cornea stroma (Hay and Revel, 1969; Noden, 1978; Lwigale et al., 2005; Creuzet et al., 2005; Feneck et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The corneal epithelium synthesizes the corneal ECM in response to inductive signals from the lens vesicle to form the primary stroma.
source: Among the initial effects of the signaling that takes place between the nascent ocular tissues is the synthesis of the corneal ECM by the corneal epithelium in response to inductive signals from the lens vesicle to form the primary stroma (Hay and Revel, 1969; Hendrix et al., 1982; Fitch et al., 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In birds and humans, the primary stroma serves as a scaffold for periocular neural crest (pNC) migration throughout the process of corneal development.
source: In birds and humans, the primary stroma serves an important role as a scaffold for periocular neural crest (pNC) migration throughout the process of corneal development (Hay and Revel, 1969; Bard and Hay, 1975; Quantock and Young, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The primary stroma consists of multiple ECM proteins, including hyaluronan, collagen type I and II, laminin, and fibronectin.
source: It consists of multiple ECM proteins, including hyaluronan (Toole and Trelstad, 1971), collagen type I and II (Hayashi et al., 1988; Fitch et al., 1988), laminin (Doane et al., 1996), and fibronectin (Fn) (Fitch et al., 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Following the second wave of pNC migration into the developing cornea, the primary stroma is concomitantly replaced by the secondary stroma that is synthesized by differentiating stromal keratocytes.
source: Following the second wave of pNC migration into the developing cornea, the primary stroma is concomitantly replaced by the secondary stroma that is synthesized by differentiating stromal keratocytes.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about corneal development.

claim: The secondary stroma comprises the bulk of the adult cornea and consists of collagens and proteoglycans.
source: The secondary stroma comprises the bulk of the adult cornea and consists of collagens and proteoglycans (Hayashi et al., 1988; Quantock and Young, 2008) that are arranged in patterns that result in transparency (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Collagens and proteoglycans in the secondary stroma are arranged in patterns that result in transparency.
source: The secondary stroma comprises the bulk of the adult cornea and consists of collagens and proteoglycans (Hayashi et al., 1988; Quantock and Young, 2008) that are arranged in patterns that result in transparency (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Early corneal development in rodents does not involve the primary stroma.
source: However, most of these studies were conducted in rodents, in which early corneal development does not involve the primary stroma (Pei and Rhodin, 1970; Haustein, 1983; Feneck et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: RNA-seq analysis of pNC differentiation into corneal cells identified novel expression and upregulation of nephronectin (Npnt) transcripts during corneal development.
source: Our recent RNA-seq analysis of pNC differentiation into corneal cells identified novel expression and upregulation of nephronectin (Npnt) transcripts during corneal development.
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to the authors' previous RNA-seq study.

claim: Npnt was discovered as an ECM ligand for integrin α8β1 (α8β1) during mouse kidney development.
source: Npnt was discovered as an ECM ligand for integrin α8β1 (α8β1) during mouse kidney development, consisting of 70–90 kDa proteins (Brandenberger et al., 2001) generated by alternate splicing (561–609 amino acids).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt consists of 70–90 kDa proteins generated by alternate splicing (561–609 amino acids).
source: Npnt was discovered as an ECM ligand for integrin α8β1 (α8β1) during mouse kidney development, consisting of 70–90 kDa proteins (Brandenberger et al., 2001) generated by alternate splicing (561–609 amino acids).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt consists of five EGF-like domains in the N-terminal, a central region containing an Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) sequence, and a meprin-A5 protein-receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase μ (MAM) domain in the C-terminal.
source: Npnt consists of five EGF-like domains in the N-terminal, a central region containing an Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) sequence, and a meprin-A5 protein-receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase μ (MAM) domain in the C-terminal.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Npnt protein structure.

claim: The RGD domain of Npnt signals through α8β1 receptor during epithelial–mesenchymal interactions involved in kidney development and maintenance.
source: The RGD domain signals through α8β1 receptor during epithelial–mesenchymal interactions involved in kidney development and maintenance (Miner, 2001; Linton et al., 2007; Müller et al., 1997; Sato et al., 2009; Cheng et al., 2008; Inagi et al., 2017; Müller-Deile et al., 2017; Zimmerman et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Recessive mutation in the Npnt gene caused bilateral kidney agenesis in human fetuses.
source: These observations in mice were recently confirmed by the identification of recessive mutation in the Npnt gene that caused bilateral kidney agenesis in human fetuses (Dai et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The EGF-like domains of Npnt are associated with inducing differentiation and proliferation in osteoblasts and dental stem cells through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways.
source: The EGF-like domains of Npnt are associated with inducing differentiation and proliferation in osteoblasts and dental stem cells through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways (Fang et al., 2010; Kahai et al., 2010; Arai et al., 2017) and to induce vascular endothelial cell migration via phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK) and p38MAPK (Kuek et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The EGF-like domains of Npnt induce vascular endothelial cell migration via phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK) and p38MAPK.
source: The EGF-like domains of Npnt are associated with inducing differentiation and proliferation in osteoblasts and dental stem cells through the activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways (Fang et al., 2010; Kahai et al., 2010; Arai et al., 2017) and to induce vascular endothelial cell migration via phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK) and p38MAPK (Kuek et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a role in heart development.
source: Recent studies have also implicated Npnt to play a role in heart development (Patra et al., 2011), attachment of the arrector pili muscle to hair follicles (Fujiwara et al., 2011), and during forelimb formation in amphibians (Abu-Daya et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a role in attachment of the arrector pili muscle to hair follicles.
source: Recent studies have also implicated Npnt to play a role in heart development (Patra et al., 2011), attachment of the arrector pili muscle to hair follicles (Fujiwara et al., 2011), and during forelimb formation in amphibians (Abu-Daya et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a role during forelimb formation in amphibians.
source: Recent studies have also implicated Npnt to play a role in heart development (Patra et al., 2011), attachment of the arrector pili muscle to hair follicles (Fujiwara et al., 2011), and during forelimb formation in amphibians (Abu-Daya et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a potential role in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
source: Other studies have also demonstrated that Npnt plays a potential role in diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Saferali et al., 2020), diabetic glomerulosclerosis (Nakatani et al., 2012), Fraser syndrome (Kiyozumi et al., 2012), and in various cancers (Magnussen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a potential role in diabetic glomerulosclerosis.
source: Other studies have also demonstrated that Npnt plays a potential role in diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Saferali et al., 2020), diabetic glomerulosclerosis (Nakatani et al., 2012), Fraser syndrome (Kiyozumi et al., 2012), and in various cancers (Magnussen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a potential role in Fraser syndrome.
source: Other studies have also demonstrated that Npnt plays a potential role in diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Saferali et al., 2020), diabetic glomerulosclerosis (Nakatani et al., 2012), Fraser syndrome (Kiyozumi et al., 2012), and in various cancers (Magnussen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt plays a potential role in various cancers.
source: Other studies have also demonstrated that Npnt plays a potential role in diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Saferali et al., 2020), diabetic glomerulosclerosis (Nakatani et al., 2012), Fraser syndrome (Kiyozumi et al., 2012), and in various cancers (Magnussen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt is undetectable in the pNC by embryonic day (E) 4.
source: Consistent with our RNA-seq data (Bi and Lwigale, 2019), we found that Npnt is undetectable in the pNC by embryonic day (E) 4 and in the presumptive corneal endothelium at E5, but it is primarily expressed in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and presumptive lens fiber cells at these time points (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Npnt is undetectable in the presumptive corneal endothelium at E5.
source: Consistent with our RNA-seq data (Bi and Lwigale, 2019), we found that Npnt is undetectable in the pNC by embryonic day (E) 4 and in the presumptive corneal endothelium at E5, but it is primarily expressed in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and presumptive lens fiber cells at these time points (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Npnt is primarily expressed in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and presumptive lens fiber cells at E4 and E5.
source: Consistent with our RNA-seq data (Bi and Lwigale, 2019), we found that Npnt is undetectable in the pNC by embryonic day (E) 4 and in the presumptive corneal endothelium at E5, but it is primarily expressed in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and presumptive lens fiber cells at these time points (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: By E6, Npnt is vividly expressed by the second wave of migratory pNC that eventually differentiate into the stromal keratocytes.
source: However, by E6, we found that in addition to the RPE and lens, Npnt is vividly expressed by the second wave of migratory pNC that eventually differentiate into the stromal keratocytes (Figure 1C, arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of Npnt persisted in the corneal stroma through E12.
source: Expression of Npnt persisted in the corneal stroma through E12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C), but it is undetectable at E15 (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Npnt is undetectable at E15.
source: Expression of Npnt persisted in the corneal stroma through E12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C), but it is undetectable at E15 (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated based on data not shown in the manuscript.

claim: At E4, Npnt protein was detected in the optic cup, lens epithelium, in the periocular mesenchyme proximal to the presumptive cornea region, and in the matrix of the primary stroma.
source: At E4, Npnt is localized in the optic cup, lens epithelium, surrounding the pNC cells adjacent to the nascent cornea (Figure 1D–F, arrow), and in the primary stroma of the cornea (Figure 1D–F, asterisk).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D–F.

claim: At E5, strong Npnt staining is observed in the primary stroma.
source: At E5, strong Npnt staining is observed in the primary stroma (Figure 1G–I, asterisk).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1G–I.

claim: By E6, vivid Npnt staining was localized in the anterior region of the cornea and diffusely throughout the primary stroma.
source: By E6, vivid Npnt staining was localized in the anterior region of the cornea and diffusely throughout the primary stroma (Figure 1J–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1J–L.

claim: At E6, the migratory pNC stained positive for Npnt.
source: At this time, the migratory pNC also stained positive for Npnt (Figure 1L, arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: Strong expression of Npnt persists in the basement membrane of the corneal epithelium through E12.
source: Strong expression of Npnt persists in the basement membrane of the corneal epithelium through (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) and is also faintly detectable in the corneal epithelial cells by E12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Npnt is faintly detectable in the corneal epithelial cells by E12.
source: Strong expression of Npnt persists in the basement membrane of the corneal epithelium through (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) and is also faintly detectable in the corneal epithelial cells by E12 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The expression of Npnt coincides with pNC ingression into the cornea.
source: Given that the changes in protein localization occur after the second wave of migration, we can conclude from our results that the expression of Npnt coincides with pNC ingression into the cornea, implicating a potential role during development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal correlation between Npnt expression and pNC migration.

claim: Knockdown of Npnt resulted in reduction of corneal thickness at E7.
source: Histological analysis of E7 corneas based on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining revealed that knockdown of Npnt (N = 4) resulted in reduction of corneal thickness (Figure 2C) compared to control (N = 5; Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining and measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: Measurements taken in the mid-corneal regions showed significant reduction in corneal thickness in Npntkd corneas.
source: Measurements taken in the mid-corneal regions (Figure 2D and E; arrowheads) showed significant reduction in corneal thickness in Npntkd corneas (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Itgα8 was expressed in the leading edge of the periocular mesenchyme prior to pNC migration into the primary stroma of the nascent cornea.
source: Our analysis by in situ hybridization revealed that Itgα8 was expressed in the leading edge of the periocular mesenchyme prior to pNC migration into the primary stroma of the nascent cornea (Figure 3A, arrow).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Itgα8 was maintained in the periocular mesenchyme but also expressed in the corneal endothelium at E5.
source: Subsequently, Itgα8 was maintained in the periocular mesenchyme but also expressed in the corneal endothelium at E5 (Figure 3B, arrows) and stroma at E6 (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Itgα8 was expressed in the stroma at E6.
source: Subsequently, Itgα8 was maintained in the periocular mesenchyme but also expressed in the corneal endothelium at E5 (Figure 3B, arrows) and stroma at E6 (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment with the α8β1 inhibitor significantly decreased the density of migratory cells from the explant.
source: In contrast, we observed that treatment with the α8β1 inhibitor significantly decreased the density of migratory cells from the explant (Figure 3F and G, Figure 3—video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: α8β1 functions as a receptor for Npnt signaling in the presumptive corneal pNC.
source: These results indicate that α8β1 functions as a receptor for Npnt signaling in the presumptive corneal pNC, and that it is required for their migration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the inhibitor experiments showing reduced migration when α8β1 is blocked.

claim: α8β1 is required for pNC migration.
source: These results indicate that α8β1 functions as a receptor for Npnt signaling in the presumptive corneal pNC, and that it is required for their migration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the inhibitor experiments showing reduced migration when α8β1 is blocked.

claim: At E5, relatively fewer GFP-positive cells expressing the Itgα8kd construct appeared to migrate into the cornea compared to RCAS-GFP control.
source: We found that at this time point relatively fewer GFP-positive cells expressing the Itgα8kd construct appeared to migrate into the cornea (Figure 4B, arrows) compared to RCAS-GFP control, which showed robust occupation of GFP-positive cells in the corneal endothelium (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by whole-mount imaging data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Histological analysis at E7 revealed reduction in corneal thickness following Itgα8 knockdown.
source: Nonetheless, histological analysis at E7 revealed reduction in corneal thickness following Itgα8 knockdown (Figure 4D) compared to control corneas (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Measurements and quantification of cells in the mid-corneal regions showed an overall significant reduction in corneal thickness and cell number, but no difference in cell density between Itgα8kd and control corneas.
source: Measurements and quantification of cells in the mid-corneal regions showed an overall significant reduction in corneal thickness and cell number, but no difference in cell density between Itgα8kd and control corneas (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 4E.

claim: BrdU assay observed no significant differences in cell proliferation between Itgα8kd and control corneas.
source: Furthermore, we performed a bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) assay and observed no significant differences in cell proliferation between Itgα8kd (Figure 4G) and control corneas (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU assay data shown in Figure 4F, G, and H.

claim: Itgα8 is required for pNC migration into the cornea.
source: These results indicate that Itgα8 is required for pNC migration into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the knockdown experiments showing reduced corneal thickness without changes in proliferation.

claim: The corneal thinning defect following knockdown of Itgα8 correlates with Npnt knockdown.
source: Given that the corneal thinning defect following knockdown of Itgα8 correlates with Npnt knockdown, our results suggest that Npnt-Itgα8 signaling plays an important role during pNC migration into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing the phenotypes of Npnt and Itgα8 knockdown.

claim: Npnt-Itgα8 signaling plays an important role during pNC migration into the cornea.
source: Given that the corneal thinning defect following knockdown of Itgα8 correlates with Npnt knockdown, our results suggest that Npnt-Itgα8 signaling plays an important role during pNC migration into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of Npnt and Itgα8 knockdown experiments.

claim: At E9, expression of Npnt was localized in the corneal stroma during normal development.
source: At E9, expression of Npnt was localized in the corneal stroma during normal development (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Npntoe corneas showed robust expression of Npnt in the stroma, as well as ectopic expression in the corneal epithelium and endothelium, and the lens.
source: However, Npntoe corneas showed robust expression of Npnt in the stroma, as well as ectopic expression in the corneal epithelium and endothelium, and the lens (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: At E9, strong staining for Npnt protein was only observed in the basement membrane of the corneal epithelium and low diffuse staining in the stroma of control corneas.
source: At this stage, strong staining for Npnt protein was only observed in the basement membrane of the corneal epithelium and low diffuse staining in the stroma of control corneas (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The Npntoe corneas showed strong ectopic staining for Npnt in the corneal epithelium and endothelium, and a substantial increase in protein expression in the stroma compared to the control.
source: In contrast, the Npntoe corneas showed strong ectopic staining for Npnt in the corneal epithelium and endothelium, and a substantial increase in protein expression in the stroma compared to the control (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Analysis did not reveal any significant differences in corneal thickness and cell number at E7 between control and Npntoe corneas.
source: Our analysis did not reveal any significant differences in corneal thickness and cell number at E7 (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Cross-sections of E9 Npntoe corneas revealed significant thickening and increase in the cell number compared with control.
source: By contrast, cross-sections of E9 Npntoe corneas revealed significant thickening and increase in the cell number (Figure 5F–H) compared with control (Figure 5C, G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining and quantitative measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: Similar increases in corneal thickness and cell number were observed at E15 in Npntoe corneas.
source: Similar increases in corneal thickness and cell number were observed at E15 (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Relatively higher cell densities were observed in the anterior stroma of E7, E9, and E15 corneas and there were no significant differences between Npntoe and control corneas.
source: Overall, we observed relatively higher cell densities in the anterior stroma of E7, E9, and E15 corneas and there were no significant differences between Npntoe and control corneas (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Posterior cell density was not affected in E7 Npntoe corneas, but there was significant reduction at E9 and E15.
source: Posterior cell density was not affected in E7 Npntoe corneas, but there was significant reduction at E9 and E15.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Cell proliferation results revealed no significant increase in cell proliferation at E7 and E15 in Npntoe corneas.
source: However, our results revealed no significant increase in cell proliferation at E7 and E15.
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU assay data shown in Figure 5J and K.

claim: There was a significant reduction in cell proliferation in E9 Npntoe corneas despite their increase in thickness.
source: Surprisingly, there was a significant reduction in cell proliferation in E9 Npntoe corneas despite their increase in thickness (Figure 5K).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU assay data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Overexpression of Npnt increases transcript and protein expression in the cornea, which results in increased cell number in the stroma and corneal thickness.
source: Combined, our data indicate that overexpression of Npnt increases transcript and protein expression in the cornea, which results in increased cell number in the stroma and corneal thickness.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of expression analysis and morphological measurements.

claim: The changes in corneal thickness following Npnt overexpression are due to augmented pNC migration into the cornea caused by excessive expression of Npnt.
source: Since these increases were not correlated with increased cell proliferation, our data suggest that the changes in corneal thickness are due to augmented pNC migration into the cornea caused by excessive expression of Npnt.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that increased thickness is not accompanied by increased proliferation.

claim: Neither the Npnt-RAE nor Npnt-EGF versions caused a significant change in corneal thickness compared with the control.
source: Contrary to our observations following overexpression of the full-length protein (Figure 5), neither the Npnt-RAE nor Npnt-EGF versions caused a significant change in corneal thickness compared with the control (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 6C.

claim: There was a significant reduction in cell count and density in Npnt-RAE corneas.
source: Interestingly, there was a significant reduction in cell count and density in Npnt-RAE corneas, although no difference in these values was observed for Npnt-EGF (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: No difference in cell count and density was observed for Npnt-EGF corneas.
source: Interestingly, there was a significant reduction in cell count and density in Npnt-RAE corneas, although no difference in these values was observed for Npnt-EGF (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: The absence of corneal thickening following overexpression of either Npnt-RAE or Npnt-EGF constructs suggests that the RGD domain plays an essential role in this process.
source: The absence of corneal thickening following overexpression of either Npnt-RAE or Npnt-EGF constructs further suggests that the RGD domain plays an essential role in this process.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that mutant and truncated Npnt do not cause corneal thickening.

claim: The EGF-like domain does not play an essential role during pNC migration into the cornea.
source: Our results also indicate that the EGF-like domain does not play an essential role during pNC migration into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the EGF-only construct does not affect corneal thickness.

claim: Inhibition of FAK reduced pNC migration from the explant but also severely attenuated cell attachment.
source: We compared explants cultured on Npnt with the inhibitor for α8β1 or FAK and observed that similar to the α8β1 inhibitor (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and D), inhibition of FAK reduced pNC migration from the explant but also severely attenuated cell attachment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: In the presence of the ROCK inhibitor, cells dissociated from the explant, attached to the Npnt substrate, and transformed into a rounded phenotype with significantly increased surface area compared to Npnt alone.
source: Under these conditions, the cells dissociated from the explant, attached to the Npnt substrate, and transformed into a rounded phenotype with significantly increased surface area compared to Npnt alone (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by explant migration assay data shown in Figure 7A–C.

claim: The ROCK inhibitor significantly decreased the density of migratory cells.
source: In addition, our analysis indicated that the ROCK inhibitor significantly decreased the density of migratory cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 7D.

claim: In the presence of the ROCK inhibitor cells exhibited a significantly reduced preferred orientation (90° ± 30°) compared to Npnt alone.
source: Our results revealed that in the presence of the ROCK inhibitor cells exhibited a significantly reduced preferred orientation (90° ± 30°) compared to Npnt alone (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 7E.

claim: In the presence of the ROCK inhibitor, the pNC spread out on the Npnt substrate with limited directional migration.
source: Thus, in the presence of the ROCK inhibitor, the pNC spread out on the Npnt substrate with limited directional migration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observations of increased cell area and reduced directional orientation.

claim: The ROCK inhibitor attenuated the formation of actin stress fibers in pNC as indicated by the substantial reduction in the intensity of phalloidin staining.
source: As previously reported (Katoh et al., 2001; Masamune et al., 2003; Takamura et al., 2001), the ROCK inhibitor attenuated the formation of actin stress fibers in pNC as indicated by the substantial reduction in the intensity of phalloidin staining (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by phalloidin staining shown in Figure 7F and G and citations to previous work.

claim: The number of pY118 paxillin puncta per cell significantly increased in the presence of the ROCK inhibitor.
source: Cells in both conditions stained positive for pY118 paxillin, but the number of puncta per cell significantly increased in the presence of the ROCK inhibitor.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Disruption of Rho kinase prevents pNC from forming the actin stress fibers and the cells adhere to the Npnt substrate using multiple foci.
source: This result indicates that disruption of Rho kinase prevents pNC from forming the actin stress fibers and that the cells adhere to the Npnt substrate using multiple foci.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observations of reduced actin stress fibers and increased focal adhesions.

claim: Npnt/Itgα8 signaling activates FAK/paxillin for adhesion.
source: Collectively, these data show that Npnt/Itgα8 signaling activates FAK/paxillin for adhesion and that the Rho signaling pathway plays an important role during pNC migration on Npnt.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of inhibitor experiments.

claim: The Rho signaling pathway plays an important role during pNC migration on Npnt.
source: Collectively, these data show that Npnt/Itgα8 signaling activates FAK/paxillin for adhesion and that the Rho signaling pathway plays an important role during pNC migration on Npnt.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of inhibitor experiments.

claim: Npnt was discovered as preosteoblast epidermal growth factor (EGF)-like repeat protein with meprin A5 protein and receptor protein-tyrosine phosphatase μ domain (POEM).
source: At the same time, it was also identified as preosteoblast epidermal growth factor (EGF)-like repeat protein with meprin A5 protein and receptor protein-tyrosine phosphatase μ domain (POEM) (Morimura et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Npnt expression in the mouse lens was observed during ocular development.
source: While Npnt is associated with kidney, teeth, and bone development (Arai et al., 2017; Kuek et al., 2016; Linton et al., 2007), only one reference was made to its expression in the mouse lens during ocular development (Brandenberger et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The lens and corneal endothelium induce the corneal epithelium to synthesize collagen and glycosaminoglycans into the underlying space.
source: The link between the primary stroma and the presumptive corneal epithelium and endothelium was established in classical studies, which showed that the lens and corneal endothelium induce the corneal epithelium to synthesize collagen and glycosaminoglycans into the underlying space (Fitch et al., 1994; Hay et al., 1979; Hay and Revel, 1969; Toole and Trelstad, 1971).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The primary stroma sequesters Npnt initially secreted by the optic cup and the lens, and exposes it to pNC during early corneal development.
source: Our expression analyses suggest that the primary stroma sequesters Npnt initially secreted by the optic cup and the lens, and exposes it to pNC during early corneal development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression patterns observed in the study.

claim: Itgα8 is expressed in the spinal cord, optic nerve, retina, urogenital and digestive systems, and in the head epidermis.
source: Itgα8 is expressed in the spinal cord, optic nerve, retina, urogenital and digestive systems, and in the head epidermis (Bossy et al., 1991; Ogawa et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: α8β1 is known to modulate epithelial–mesenchymal interactions during kidney and pharyngeal development.
source: α8β1 is known to modulate epithelial–mesenchymal interactions during kidney and pharyngeal development (Müller et al., 1997; Talbot et al., 2016) and promote migration of mesangial and smooth muscle cells (Bieritz et al., 2003; Zargham and Thibault, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: α8β1 promotes migration of mesangial and smooth muscle cells.
source: α8β1 is known to modulate epithelial–mesenchymal interactions during kidney and pharyngeal development (Müller et al., 1997; Talbot et al., 2016) and promote migration of mesangial and smooth muscle cells (Bieritz et al., 2003; Zargham and Thibault, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Itgα8 heterodimerizes with Itgβ1 subunit.
source: Since Itgα8 heterodimerizes with Itgβ1 subunit (Bossy et al., 1991), which is robustly expressed in the periocular mesenchyme and migratory pNC (Doane and Birk, 1994), we infer that α8β1 signaling functions during corneal development in response to Npnt secreted in the primary stroma.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Itgβ1 is robustly expressed in the periocular mesenchyme and migratory pNC.
source: Since Itgα8 heterodimerizes with Itgβ1 subunit (Bossy et al., 1991), which is robustly expressed in the periocular mesenchyme and migratory pNC (Doane and Birk, 1994), we infer that α8β1 signaling functions during corneal development in response to Npnt secreted in the primary stroma.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: α8β1 signaling functions during corneal development in response to Npnt secreted in the primary stroma.
source: Since Itgα8 heterodimerizes with Itgβ1 subunit (Bossy et al., 1991), which is robustly expressed in the periocular mesenchyme and migratory pNC (Doane and Birk, 1994), we infer that α8β1 signaling functions during corneal development in response to Npnt secreted in the primary stroma.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression patterns and known interactions.

claim: Following delamination from the neural tube, cranial neural crest migrate in response to Fn and laminin via integrin receptors such as α1β1, α4β1, α5β1, and αVβ1.
source: Following delamination from the neural tube, cranial neural crest migrate in response to Fn and laminin (Duband and Thiery, 1982; Newgreen and Thiery, 1980; Sternberg and Kimber, 1986) via integrin receptors such as α1β1, α4β1, α5β1, and αVβ1 (Alfandari et al., 2003; Delannet et al., 1994; Desban and Duband, 1997; Kil et al., 1996; Lallier et al., 1994).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Neural crest cells are initially highly migratory, but they remain relatively stationary upon their localization in the periocular region.
source: Although neural crest cells are initially highly migratory, they remain relatively stationary upon their localization in the periocular region.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about neural crest cell behavior.

claim: Itgα8 expression coincides with the onset of pNC migration.
source: Given that Itgα8 expression coincides with the onset of pNC migration, our results indicate its potential role in their ingression into the developing cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal correlation between Itgα8 expression and pNC migration.

claim: The three major factors that contribute to corneal thickness during development are pNC migration, cell proliferation, and synthesis of the secondary stroma by the keratocytes.
source: The three major factors that contribute to corneal thickness during development are pNC migration, cell proliferation, and synthesis of the secondary stroma by the keratocytes.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about corneal development.

claim: Npnt has been shown to promote migration in various tissues, including vascular endothelial cells during osteogenesis, infiltration of immune cells into the liver, and cancer metastasis.
source: In addition to functioning in epithelial–mesenchymal interactions, Npnt has been shown to promote migration in various tissues, including vascular endothelial cells during osteogenesis (Kuek et al., 2016), infiltration of immune cells into the liver (Hong et al., 2020; Inagaki et al., 2013), and cancer metastasis (Magnussen et al., 2020; Mei et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The primary function of keratocytes is to synthesize the corneal ECM comprising collagens and proteoglycans, which represents approximately 90% of the corneal thickness.
source: Given that the primary function of keratocytes is to synthesize the corneal ECM comprising collagens and proteoglycans, and represents approximately 90% of the corneal thickness (Fini, 1999; Funderburgh et al., 2003; Kao, 2010), our observation that there was no change in stromal cell density raises a possibility that matrix synthesis by the pNC that differentiated into keratocytes is not a major contributing factor to the reduction in corneal thickness.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Matrix synthesis by the pNC that differentiated into keratocytes is not a major contributing factor to the reduction in corneal thickness following Npnt knockdown.
source: Given that the primary function of keratocytes is to synthesize the corneal ECM comprising collagens and proteoglycans, and represents approximately 90% of the corneal thickness (Fini, 1999; Funderburgh et al., 2003; Kao, 2010), our observation that there was no change in stromal cell density raises a possibility that matrix synthesis by the pNC that differentiated into keratocytes is not a major contributing factor to the reduction in corneal thickness.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that cell density is unchanged despite reduced thickness.

claim: Increased corneal thickness following Npnt overexpression persisted at E15 when Npnt appears to be downregulated in the cornea.
source: We also found that increased corneal thickness persisted at E15 when Npnt appears to be downregulated in the cornea.
evidence: The claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The E7 corneas were not affected in the overexpression studies possibly due to limited pNC migration potential caused by their expression of Neuropilin1, which prevents them from entering the corneal environment that contains a repulsive Semaphorin3A signal.
source: Surprisingly, the E7 corneas were not affected in the overexpression studies. This could be caused by limited pNC migration potential due to their expression of Neuropilin1, which prevents them from entering the corneal environment that contains a repulsive Semaphorin3A signal (Lwigale and Bronner-Fraser, 2009).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on previous work about Neuropilin1/Semaphorin3A signaling.

claim: The mutant Npnt with RAE domain may outcompete the expression of the endogenous RGD by the pNC, leading to reduction in cell count and density.
source: The reduction in cell count and density could be attributed to the mutant RAE domain outcompeting the expression of the endogenous RGD by the pNC.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning to explain the observed reduction in cell count and density.

claim: Both α5β1 and α8β1 activate the Rho/Rock pathway.
source: Given that pNC migrate on both Fn and Npnt in vitro, and that both α5β1 and α8β1 activate the Rho/Rock pathway (Benoit et al., 2009; Danen et al., 2005; White et al., 2007; Zargham et al., 2007), it is possible that Rho activity increases as the cells migrate from the periocular region into the matrix of the developing cornea due to the presence of additional cues from Npnt.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Rho activity may increase as the cells migrate from the periocular region into the matrix of the developing cornea due to the presence of additional cues from Npnt.
source: Given that pNC migrate on both Fn and Npnt in vitro, and that both α5β1 and α8β1 activate the Rho/Rock pathway (Benoit et al., 2009; Danen et al., 2005; White et al., 2007; Zargham et al., 2007), it is possible that Rho activity increases as the cells migrate from the periocular region into the matrix of the developing cornea due to the presence of additional cues from Npnt.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the combined effects of Fn and Npnt signaling.

claim: Disruptions in the sequence of early events during corneal development can lead to significant defects in corneal development.
source: Precise coordination of multiple signals from surrounding ocular tissues orchestrates the spatiotemporal migration and differentiation of multipotent pNC during the formation of the avian corneal endothelium and stromal keratocytes. Disruptions in the sequence of these early events can lead to significant defects in corneal development.
evidence: This is based on general knowledge about developmental processes.

claim: Despite being surrounded by an ECM rich in Fn, pNC remain relatively immobile in the periocular region until some become competent to respond to Npnt cues via the expression of α8β1.
source: Despite being surrounded by an ECM rich in Fn, pNC remain relatively immobile in the periocular region until some become competent to respond to Npnt cues via the expression of α8β1.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression patterns and migration behavior observed in the study.

claim: The transformation of pNC to express α8β1 may be crucial for the timely induction of directional migration of pNC towards the gradient of additional cues generated by Npnt in the primary stroma.
source: This transformation may be crucial for the timely induction of directional migration of pNC towards the gradient of additional cues generated by Npnt in the primary stroma (Figure 8A and B), and therefore plays a vital role in segregating the cornea progenitors from the rest of the periocular mesenchyme.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression patterns and migration behavior, and illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Npnt plays a vital role in segregating the cornea progenitors from the rest of the periocular mesenchyme.
source: This transformation may be crucial for the timely induction of directional migration of pNC towards the gradient of additional cues generated by Npnt in the primary stroma (Figure 8A and B), and therefore plays a vital role in segregating the cornea progenitors from the rest of the periocular mesenchyme.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of the study.

claim: Npnt protein subsequently localizes to the basement membrane of the epithelial layer.
source: Our observation that the Npnt protein subsequently localizes to the basement membrane of the epithelial layer, combined with its pleiotropic functions during development and in disease (Yamada and Kamijo, 2016), implies that Npnt may have other functions at later stages of cornea development.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Npnt may have other functions at later stages of cornea development.
source: Our observation that the Npnt protein subsequently localizes to the basement membrane of the epithelial layer, combined with its pleiotropic functions during development and in disease (Yamada and Kamijo, 2016), implies that Npnt may have other functions at later stages of cornea development.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the localization pattern and known functions of Npnt.

claim: Npnt may mediate epithelial–mesenchymal interactions between the cornea epithelium and stroma by signaling through the EGF-like domain to EGFRs in the epithelial cells.
source: One possibility is that Npnt mediates epithelial–mesenchymal interactions between the cornea epithelium and stroma by signaling through the EGF-like domain to EGFRs in the epithelial cells.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about potential functions of Npnt at later stages.

claim: All pNC cells express α5β1.
source: We posit that all pNC cells express α5β1 and previously showed that they robustly migrate on Fn substrate in vitro (Lwigale and Bronner-Fraser, 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' previous work.

claim: pNC robustly migrate on Fn substrate in vitro.
source: We posit that all pNC cells express α5β1 and previously showed that they robustly migrate on Fn substrate in vitro (Lwigale and Bronner-Fraser, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: In vivo, the pNC which express both α5β1 and α8β1, and thus can respond to Npnt and Fn, migrate into the cornea.
source: However, in vivo, it is most likely that the pNC, which express both α5β1 and α8β1, and thus can respond to Npnt and Fn, migrate into the cornea.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the expression patterns and migration behavior observed in the study.

claim: Npnt/Itgα8 signaling plays an essential role in pNC migration during corneal development.
source: Based on this study, we conclude that Npnt/Itgα8 signaling plays an essential role in pNC migration during corneal development.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental results.

claim: Npnt appears in an increasing gradient from the periocular region into the cornea at E5.
source: Npnt appears in an increasing gradient from the periocular region into the cornea, whereas Fn stains both the periocular mesenchyme and cornea.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Fn stains both the periocular mesenchyme and cornea at E5.
source: Npnt appears in an increasing gradient from the periocular region into the cornea, whereas Fn stains both the periocular mesenchyme and cornea.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: A subpopulation of pNC that reside in the region adjacent to the presumptive cornea express both α5β1 and α8β1.
source: All pNC respond to Fn via expression of α5β1, but a subpopulation of pNC that reside in the region adjacent to the presumptive cornea express both α5β1 and α8β1, and become competent to also read the additional gradient of Npnt in the ECM, thus migrating into the corneal region.
evidence: The claim is illustrated in the model shown in Figure 8B.

claim: pNC that express both α5β1 and α8β1 become competent to read the additional gradient of Npnt in the ECM, thus migrating into the corneal region.
source: All pNC respond to Fn via expression of α5β1, but a subpopulation of pNC that reside in the region adjacent to the presumptive cornea express both α5β1 and α8β1, and become competent to also read the additional gradient of Npnt in the ECM, thus migrating into the corneal region.
evidence: The claim is the proposed model illustrated in Figure 8B based on the study's findings.
